articles.title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth
articles.summary: Sir Ed Davey pledged to spend £600m a year on maternity services if the Lib Dems were in government.
articles.body:
Liberal Democrats are calling for one-to-one midwife care for women in labour, as figures suggest life-altering childbirth injuries in England have reached record levels.

Lib Dem analysis of NHS figures showed the number of women suffering potentially life-threatening levels of blood loss is the highest ever recorded in England.

Three in every 100 women suffered serious tearing injuries requiring emergency surgery in the first half of this year, something party leader Sir Ed Davey said was a "devastating indictment of our NHS maternity services".

The government is expected to publish a new national maternity and neonatal action plan by the end of the year.

Speaking to BBC Breakfast at the Lib Dem annual conference in Brighton, Davey pledged to spend £600m a year on maternity services if in government.

He said £1.3bn a year was currently being spent on "failure" through negligence compensation payouts for poor maternity services, but said this investment should go towards prevention instead.

Calling for more senior midwives and consultants, he said: "Our current maternity staff are run ragged - they're massively overstretched.

"That's the best way, all the evidence shows, to make sure maternity units are safe," he added.

"It is a scandal at the moment - we've seen inquiry after inquiry. So many women are suffering injuries at birth and we're seeing the loss of babies too; it is a tragedy as well as a scandal."

He said ministers "cannot turn a blind eye to this national safety scandal" and mothers "deserve safe, compassionate care".

The Lib Dems are calling for a consultant obstetrician to be present on every labour ward at all hours, one-to-one midwifery care for every woman in labour, and recruit an extra 300 consultant midwives.

The party pointed to Care Quality Commission (CQC) survey data showing one-in-10 women, about 54,000, were left alone during late stages of labour or childbirth last year, which the Lib Dems said was due to lack of training and staff shortages.

More than 8,000 women had postpartum haemorrhages with blood loss of more than 1.5l since the start of this year, more than double the number over the equivalent period in 2021, the party's analysis of NHS figures suggests.

Rates of major haemorrhage peaked between April and June this year, while 32.7 women per thousand needed emergency treatment.

The rate of third or fourth degree vaginal tears during childbirth has risen by 29% in the last five years, according to the analysis.

The Lib Dem health spokesperson Helen Morgan, who successfully campaigned for an independent maternity commissioner to drive improvements, said reports on previous maternity scandals were "gathering dust".

"Years after the Shrewsbury and Telford scandal which devastated my community - my neighbours and friends - women continue to suffer," she said.

"This must be the moment we say 'enough'."

A review in 2022 found catastrophic failures at Shrewsbury and Telford NHS Trust (SaTH) over 20 years may have led to the deaths of more than 200 babies.

The trust apologised and said it had already put in measures to prevent a repeat.

A Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) spokesperson said the review to be published later this year will bring together the recommendations from the Baroness Amos, Donna Ockenden, and Lady Justice Thirlwall inquiries, set clear priorities and hold the system to account for delivering improved outcomes.

"Every woman deserves safe maternity care and the new health secretary has made this issue a personal priority," they said.

"Through the National Maternity and Neonatal Taskforce that she is chairing, this government will deliver the reforms needed to ensure the very highest standards of safety and care for every mother and baby."

England's first statutory Maternity and Neonatal Commissioner will be appointed to ensure the voices of women, babies and families are at the heart of national policy making.

The DHSC is also extending Martha's Rule to every maternity and neonatal ward to ensure that any reports of deterioration from patients or their families are acted upon, and has invested £187m since April 2025 to address critical safety risks in the maternity and neonatal estate.

A Labour Party spokesperson said: "Ed Davey was part of the coalition government that tore up the national standards for maternity services that Yvette Cooper is now having to restore.

"He never raised any objections to that decision at the time, and he has never apologised since. Until he does so, his words on this issue will ring hollow."

Addressing the criticism of Julian Brazil, Leader of Devon County Council , the party who said on Sunday he thought the party was "sleepwalking into irrelevance" , Sir Ed told BBC Breakfast there was always going to be criticism of leadership as the party gets bigger.

"We have grown really fast under my leadership , with record number of MPs and running more councils," he said.

"When you have a bigger party you can't please everyone all the time."

articles.title: D-Day veteran Kenneth Hay dies aged 101
articles.summary: Kenneth Hay was an "extraordinary gentleman whose remarkable life will never be forgotten", the British Normandy Memorial says.
articles.body:
Normandy veteran Kenneth Hay, who survived being captured just weeks after D-Day and spent years educating children about World War Two, has died aged 101.

Hay, from Upminster in east London, served in the 4th Dorset Infantry Regiment. He was captured a month after the allied invasion of northern France and survived a 1,000-mile (1,609km) forced march in eastern Europe until he was liberated by US forces.

His death was announced on Sunday by the British Normandy Memorial, for which he was an ambassador.

The organisation said he was an "extraordinary gentleman whose remarkable life will never be forgotten".

In its statement on social media, the British Normandy Memorial added: "His passion for education was unwavering.

"The countless schoolchildren whose lives he touched with his stories of courage and resilience nicknamed him 'Grandad Ken'.

"We extend our most sincere condolences to Ken's sons Chris and Jeremy, all the Hay family and his very many friends."

D-Day, on 6 June 1944, saw British, American and Canadian troops storm beaches along the Normandy coastline to begin the liberation of France from Nazi occupation.

Hay had landed at Courseulles-sur-Mer just days after and was captured by the German 12th SS Panzer Division during a night patrol on 7-8 July.

He was taken to Zabrze in Poland, where he was put to work as a prisoner of war in a coal mine.

Speaking of the capture in 2024, Hay recalled his first feelings were of "dread" and "fear".

"We went out on night patrol, was supposed to be doing a blow up of a self-propelled gun in no man's land, but in fact, it was behind their lines," he said.

"So they let us through and then very unfriendly, they sealed it and wouldn't let us back, so we had a battle.

"We had 30 [that] went out on our patrol, 16 including my brother, who was a corporal, got back, five of us got captured and then presumably nine got killed."

As the Russians approached, the prisoners were marched to a new location, approximately 1,000 miles away, during which many of them died.

During the three-month march, Hay said he once "lay down to die" after it became too painful to continue, but two friends turned back for him and lifted him with an "arm around each shoulder".

Eventually they were liberated by American troops and Hay returned to the UK, via Reims, on 4 May 1945.

Recalling the moment he made it to his mother's house in Barking, he said: "They came running down the road to greet me."

After the war, he was appointed an MBE for services to the community and received the Legion d'Honneur, France's highest order of merit.

Hay regularly visited British schools to share stories of the war and answer questions, saying he believed it was his "duty to pass it on".

articles.title: Meet Kiran Ahirwar, the ‘Drone Didi’ from Guna, Madhya Pradesh who became a Lakhpati Didi and is inspiring village women; “Mujhe gaon ki mahila nahi, plane ki pilot dikh rahi thi”
articles.summary: When Union minister Jyotiraditya Scindia recently took the controls of an agricultural drone in a village, Madhya Pradesh, it was not just the machine.
articles.body: When Union minister Jyotiraditya Scindia recently took the controls of an agricultural drone in a village, Madhya Pradesh, it was not just the machine that caught attention. Standing beside him was Kiran Ahirwar, a woman from Guna's Pagara village who had taught herself to be an expert with technology that is still new in India's rural regions.Meet Kiran Ahirwar who is getting media attention and politician praise for all the right reasons. On September 18, Kiran demonstrated how she operates an agricultural drone during Scindia's visit to Barkheda Gird in Guna.The Union minister watched her in awe operate the drone, flew it himself under her guidance and then praised her openly. According to DD News, Scindia praised Kiran's technical proficiency and confidence.Addressing the media and the crowd, the minister said, “Kiran ne aaj apna hunar dikhaya aur puri tarah se apne NaMo Drone Didi ka jacket pehen ke, topi pehen ke. Mujhe gaon ki mahila nahi dikh rahi thi, mujhe to plane ki pilot dikh rahi thi.”(“Kiran demonstrated her skills today, wearing her NaMo Drone Didi jacket and cap. I couldn’t see a village woman; I could see a pilot flying a plane.”)Who is Kiran Ahirwar?For Kiran, learning to fly a drone is only one part of her bigger journey. She is known as a ‘Namo Drone Didi’ and a ‘Lakhpati Didi’. These two identities together tell the story of how women in rural India are moving beyond traditional livelihood activities. Kiran’s story is one of the best examples of how women across rural regions are inspired to start their own businesses and earn their own money.Entering the world of dronesKiran is a member of the Vansh Self-Help Group in Pagara village, under the Madhya Pradesh State Rural Livelihood Mission. Her journey began with vermicomposting and organic farming. These activities helped her build an income and eventually become a Lakhpati Didi.Then she entered the NaMo Didi Drone Yojna. Her work includes operating an agricultural drone. As per several media reports, Kiran earns nearly ₹12,000 to ₹15,000 a month through her different livelihood activities, including vermicomposting, organic farming and work connected with the Namo Drone initiative.Government’s ‘Drone Didi’ initiativeKiran received a drone under the Prime Minister Women Farmer Drone Centre initiative and underwent 10 days of free training in Bhopal and Indore. The idea behind the government's Namo Drone Didi scheme is to train women from self-help groups to operate drones and provide agricultural services to farmers, including the spraying of fertilisers and pesticides.Kiran now shares her knowledge with other farmers. Reports identify her as a master trainer who has taught more than 125 farmers about organic farming. Today, she is more than a drone operator. She is becoming someone other women and farmers can approach to learn new ways of doing things.Meeting ScindiaIn Barkheda Gird, Kiran stood in a field and demonstrated the drone's operation before the Union minister. Scindia then took the controls himself. That is perhaps the most powerful part of the Drone Didi story.Kiran's journey does not suggest that women have to leave farming or village life behind to enter the technology sector. Instead, it shows how technology can become an extension of rural livelihoods.Kiran's journey teaches us that a woman working in a village can become a farmer, entrepreneur, trainer and technology operator.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: US on alert after China's 'dual-use' research vessels spotted near Alaska multiple times this year
articles.summary: US News: The US said it is observing increased activity of Chinese research vessels around the arctic offshores of Alaska, raising mineral and security concern.
articles.body: The US said it is observing increased activity of Chinese research vessels around the arctic offshores of Alaska, raising mineral and security concerns.These research vessels have been reportedly observed close to the maritime zones near Alaska's Aleutian Islands, into the Bering Strait between the US and Russia, and as far as the North Pole.Four Chinese research vessels have conducted work offshore in the US Arctic since the beginning of 2026, compared to a total of five last year, according to commander of US Coast Guard's Arctic District, Rear Admiral Bob Little, cited by Reuters.While the Chinese ships remain in international waters, they do not notify their presence in advance as usual practise done through diplomatic channels, raising suspicion."Where I have responsibility, interest and concern is when they are operating in and around US sovereign space," said Little, adding that the vessels usually mention their purpose as scientific research or operations in international waters.Hybrid vesselsChina reportedly has the world's largest fleet of civilian research vessels that survey the Earth’s oceans.According to Center for Strategic and International Studies, a Washington based think tank, While these ships support scientific and commercial objectives, they are also being used to advance Beijing’s strategic ambitions.Many vessels that claim to undertake missions for peaceful purposes may also be capable of providing the PLA with critical information that can be either used against its adversaries.Washington is concerned that Beijing could be involved in scientific research focused on the mineral exploitation of the seabed in US regions, Little said, adding that such activities could "provide them (the Chinese) with a military advantage or pose a security threat to the United States".China calls itself a "near-Arctic" state and wants to create a "Polar Silk Road" in the Arctic, has stepped up its presence in the polar region in recent years.Indian concernsSuch threats are not limited to the arctic. Chinese research and survey vessels have been docking at Sri Lankan port of Hambantota, have raised security concerns in India because of their proximity and the ability to conduct oceanographic, seabed and satellite-tracking activities.The 2022 visit of the Chinese tracking vessel Yuan Wang 5 to Hambantota drew particular attention, while the research vessel Shi Yan 6’s 2023 visit to Colombo prompted Sri Lanka to impose a temporary moratorium on foreign research vessels. More recently, Reuters reported that Chinese research vessels have conducted extensive surveys across the Indian Ocean, including waters between Sri Lanka and Indonesia and approaches to the Malacca Strait, collecting seabed and oceanographic data that can have potential military applications.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Three people have been arrested on Monday by police in Bihar's Jamui district in connection with the alleged harassment of a minor boy and girl, after a video of the incident went viral on social media.While talking to media, Jamui SP Bishwajeet Dayal said the incident took place on the evening of September 19 and an SIT headed by Sub-Divisional Police Officer Deepti Monali has been formed to identify and arrest all those involved."Although the incident is two days old, no complaint was made before us by the boy or the girl till Sunday. Today, when the video went viral, we traced the victims with the help of the registration number of a vehicle visible in the clip," Dayal told reporters.Police said the victims did not name any accused in the FIR. However, investigators have identified around seven people from the video. Three have been arrested and raids are underway, news agency PTI reported.The SP said the person allegedly seen behaving indecently with the girl in the video has also been identified and police are making efforts to arrest him.Case registered under POCSOThe FIR has been registered under the POCSO Act and relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Police have also initiated steps to remove the video from social media platforms.Dayal said the boy and girl were friends and attended the same coaching institute, however, declined to share further details, citing the need to protect sensitive information concerning the minors.The purported video shows a group of people stopping and harassing the boy and girl by the roadside. articles.title: Bristol Airport flights grounded over air traffic control failure
articles.summary: A number of flights at Bristol Airport have been delayed or cancelled due to a technical fault.
articles.body:
A number of flights at Bristol Airport have been delayed or cancelled due to a technical failure with air traffic control systems.

A Bristol Airport spokesperson said the disruption is being caused by a "connectivity issue" at the National Air Traffic Services (Nats) at Prestwick Centre in Scotland.

Both the arrival and departure boards indicate delays of up to two hours, alongside cancelled flights to destinations including Barcelona, Nice and Edinburgh.

In a statement, Nats confirmed the issue was now fixed and said it was working with airports to lift air traffic restrictions as soon as possible.

It comes after a disruption earlier this month, caused by a "software defect" that left 2000 flights grounded across the country.

Becky Freeman became stranded at Bristol Airport after her flight to Edinburgh for a business meeting was cancelled. She described the atmosphere as "chaos".

"I was caught up in the Nats issue earlier this month and spent nine hours at Bristol airport," she said.

"I can't believe it's happened again. It is very frustrating and I will have to attempt the business meeting again for a third time."

Airports across the UK are reporting varying degrees of disruption including Glasgow, Aberdeen, Manchester, Newcastle, Liverpool, London City and Belfast City.

"Customers should check with their airlines for latest information on their flight."

A spokesperson for Nats confirmed the issue at the Prestwick Centre is "now fixed".

"We are working with airports and airlines to safely lift air traffic regulations as quickly as we can to minimise any further disruption," they added.

articles.title: At 78, Nashville songwriter Jerry Vandiver spends hundreds of volunteer hours trapping foxes sick with mange; the wildlife rescue he supports has already treated more than 60 foxes this year
articles.summary: US News: For one Nashville songwriter, answering a call for help can mean getting out of bed in the middle of the night and heading into the woods. At 78, Jerr.
articles.body: For one Nashville songwriter, answering a call for help can mean getting out of bed in the middle of the night and heading into the woods. At 78, Jerry Vandiver has spent the past seven years volunteering to rescue red foxes suffering from mange around Nashville, Tennessee. In a report, The Tennessean detailed how the singer-songwriter traps sick foxes, transports them to Walden’s Puddle Wildlife Center of Greater Nashville and later helps return them to the wild. Vandiver logged 234 volunteer hours in August alone, while Walden’s Puddle had already rehabilitated more than 60 red foxes by early September, surpassing the 44 it treated throughout all of 2025.A growing rescue effort for Nashville’s foxesVandiver’s work begins when residents spot foxes showing signs of mange. People send him photographs or contact him through Facebook, often asking for help when they see an animal with large patches of missing fur, sores or other signs of the disease. Mange is caused by microscopic skin mites. In foxes, the condition can lead to intense irritation, hair loss, scabbing and open wounds. Without treatment, weakened animals can develop secondary infections and eventually die. The disease is also contagious, making affected foxes a concern for local wildlife populations.For Vandiver, however, the presence of mange does not mean an animal is beyond saving. He has developed a routine for locating and trapping the foxes before transporting them to Walden’s Puddle for professional care. “I’m not the hero, I’m just the ambulance driver,” Vandiver told The Tennessean, explaining that mange is treatable if the animals can be caught and taken for care.He monitors foxes around NashvilleThe rescue work can take considerably more than simply setting a trap. Vandiver uses trail cameras to monitor foxes and understand their movements. Once he identifies an animal that appears to have mange, he works out where to place a trap and what bait to use. The process can take days or even weeks, depending on the animal.When a fox finally enters a trap, Vandiver does not necessarily wait until morning to deal with it. He has said that frightened foxes can injure themselves by repeatedly throwing themselves against the wire enclosure. Instead, he covers the trap with a sheet to help calm the animal, then transports it to Walden’s Puddle. There, the fox is transferred into a crate with food, water and bedding while the rescue centre’s medical staff prepares to treat it. According to Walden’s Puddle animal care manager Joanna Johnson, Vandiver has sent messages about newly trapped foxes at 2 a.m., reflecting how frequently the work extends into the night.234 volunteer hours in one monthThe scale of Vandiver’s commitment has grown alongside the number of sick foxes he encounters. In August 2026 alone, he recorded 234 volunteer hours. By early September, he and other volunteers had already captured more than 60 foxes during the year. That compares with 44 red foxes rehabilitated by Walden’s Puddle during the entire 2025 calendar year. The increase has made 2026 a particularly busy year for the rescue organisation and its volunteers.Vandiver has also become increasingly recognisable among Nashville residents. His social-media presence has expanded as he shares photographs and videos documenting foxes before and after treatment. Good News Network reported that his Facebook following grew from about 325 people to around 5,000 as his rescue work attracted wider attention.From country songwriting to wildlife rescueVandiver's life in Nashville did not begin with wildlife rehabilitation. He is a longtime singer-songwriter whose work has been recorded by country artists including Tim McGraw, Phil Vassar and Barbara Mandrell. He has also maintained a career as a performer, author and educator. His wildlife work developed alongside that career. For about seven years, he has volunteered with Walden’s Puddle, eventually becoming a regular responder for residents who encounter sick foxes.His experience has also given him a detailed understanding of the animals. Foxes generally live in family groups and require sizeable territories. As development reduces available habitat, foxes can increasingly come into contact with one another or move through areas occupied by other groups, circumstances that can facilitate the spread of contagious diseases such as mange. Good News Network, citing the rescue organisation, also noted concerns about rat poison, which can weaken animals and contribute to their vulnerability.The goal is to put them back where they belongThe trapping itself is only the first stage of the process. After treatment and recovery at Walden’s Puddle, the foxes are eventually returned to the wild. One recent release illustrated the outcome of the effort. A male fox that Vandiver had trapped after a resident reported it had been in extremely poor condition, with much of its fur missing and its skin covered in sores. Nearly three months later, its coat had grown back and its wounds had healed. Vandiver released the recovered fox back into a wooded Nashville area.For Vandiver, those releases provide a reason to continue despite the long hours. He has described watching a recovered fox disappear into the woods after being released, sometimes looking back briefly before continuing on its way. At 78, the Nashville songwriter is therefore spending much of his time away from recording studios and stages, responding to another kind of call. His work does not replace the veterinary treatment provided by Walden’s Puddle, but it helps bridge the crucial gap between an injured animal being spotted and reaching professional care.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nandigram bypoll: Congress candidate Milan Pradhan sent to judicial custody till October 5 in 2007 agitation case
articles.summary: India News: Congress' Nandigram bypoll nominee Milan Pradhan was on Monday remanded to judicial custody till October 5 in connection with a case registered at Khe.
articles.body: Congress' Nandigram bypoll nominee Milan Pradhan was on Monday remanded to judicial custody till October 5 in connection with a case registered at Khejuri Police Station 19 years ago, dealing a setback to his campaign for the October 6 assembly bypoll.Pradhan was sent to judicial custody by a Contai court in West Bengal's Purba Medinipur district, his counsel Ayan Bhattacharjee said. He added that the order would be challenged before the Calcutta high court.The development came two days after a Haldia court had remanded Pradhan to judicial custody till October 3, following his arrest on September 18 on multiple charges, including murder, linked to the 2007 Nandigram land agitation.The latest order effectively prevents Pradhan from campaigning during the final days of the bypoll campaign, which ends on October 4.The Nandigram seat was vacated by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari, who resigned in May and chose to retain Bhabanipur after defeating Mamata Banerjee in the assembly election held earlier this year.Meanwhile, Banerjee's decision to support Pradhan has marked a significant political shift between the Trinamool Congress and Congress in Bengal. Banerjee backed the Congress candidate after her faction's nominee, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew from the October 6 contest following a meeting with Adhikari in Kolkata.Announcing her support on September 18, Banerjee described Congress as a "sister party" and a "natural ally", saying the decision was taken in the larger interest of the country and to strengthen the INDIA bloc.Banerjee also said she wanted to send a message about the future of the opposition alliance beginning from Bengal.The move follows a series of political developments involving the TMC. The Election Commission had frozen the Trinamool Congress' traditional name and ‘Jora Ghash Phul’ symbol amid an internal party dispute, assigning separate names and symbols to Banerjee's faction and its dissidents for the upcoming bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar.The Congress-TMC relationship has previously seen periods of cooperation. The parties contested the 2001 Bengal assembly election together and later joined hands in the 2009 Lok Sabha polls. articles.title: São Paulo pays tribute to Paralympic athletes against Internacional
articles.summary: This Saturday (19), São Paulo carried out an initiative to honor and recognize athletes who represent the club in Paralympic sports.Before the match against...
articles.body:
This Saturday (19), São Paulo carried out an initiative to honor and recognize athletes who represent the club in Paralympic sports.

Before the match against Internacional, in the 28th round of the Brazilian Championship, the MorumBIS athletics track hosted a lap of honor featuring 10 athletes representing the APNH/SPFC project, a partnership between Tricolor and the Novo Horizonte Parasports Association.

The joint project began in 2024 with the swimming team. The following year, the partnership expanded to other sports, including athletics, powerlifting, karate, triathlon, sport shooting, and archery.

More than 150 athletes are already part of the APNH/SPFC team. Among them are standout names such as Edênia Garcia (a four-time world swimming champion, as well as winner of two silver medals and one bronze at the Paralympic Games) and Miguel Rodrigues dos Santos (ranked first in the world in the 100m freestyle swimming event).

The initiative took place on Saturday precisely because of its proximity to important dates for raising awareness of this cause. On September 21, Brazil marks the National Day of Struggle for People with Disabilities, and the following day, the 22nd, National Paralympic Athlete Day is celebrated.

São Paulo's goal with the initiative is not only to pay tribute to the athletes who represent the club, but also to reinforce the idea that sport is the best tool for inclusion, opportunity, and a sense of belonging.
